what: Fully managed, serverless service that gives API access to foundation models from Amazon, Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, Cohere, AI21, Stability AI and others, plus tools to customize and govern them.
use: build a generative AI application on top of third-party foundation models without managing any infrastructure
switch between foundation models from several providers through a single API
not: Train a classic tabular ML model such as XGBoost from your own Python code (use SageMaker)
Run speech-to-text transcription of call recordings (use Transcribe)
cue: "foundation model via API", "serverless", "no infrastructure", "multiple model providers"
vs: SageMaker JumpStart also offers FMs but deploys them to endpoints you manage.

what: Managed Retrieval Augmented Generation: connects data sources (S3, web, Confluence, SharePoint, Salesforce), chunks and embeds documents into a vector store, and retrieves relevant passages with citations at query time.
use: let an FM answer questions from the company's own internal documents with the least operational overhead
ground chatbot answers in frequently changing policy documents without retraining
not: Change the model's writing style permanently (use fine-tuning)
Call external APIs to take actions such as booking (use Agents)
vs: Fine-tuning changes weights; Knowledge Bases inject context at query time.

what: Builds autonomous assistants that break a request into steps, call APIs through action groups (Lambda + OpenAPI schema), query knowledge bases and keep session memory.
use: build an assistant that completes multi-step tasks such as checking inventory and placing an order through company APIs
automate a workflow where the FM must decide which internal API to call
not: Only filter harmful content (use Guardrails)
Simply answer questions from documents (Knowledge Bases alone is enough)
vs: Knowledge Bases retrieve; Agents act.

what: Configurable safeguards applied to prompts and responses for any FM: content filters, denied topics, word filters, sensitive information (PII) filters, contextual grounding checks and prompt-attack detection.
use: prevent a customer chatbot from giving investment advice or discussing competitors
mask personally identifiable information in model responses
block prompt-injection and jailbreak attempts
not: Explain why a tabular model made a prediction (use SageMaker Clarify)
Encrypt data at rest (use KMS)
cue: "block harmful content", "denied topics", "redact PII in responses", "responsible AI for chatbots"
vs: Clarify = bias and explainability for ML models; Guardrails = runtime safety for gen-AI.

what: Compares and scores foundation models using automatic metrics (accuracy, robustness, toxicity), human work teams, or LLM-as-a-judge, on built-in or custom prompt datasets.
use: choose the best FM for a use case by comparing candidates on accuracy and toxicity
have a human team rate model responses for brand tone and helpfulness
not: Monitor drift of a deployed SageMaker model (use Model Monitor)
Label training data (use Ground Truth)
cue: "compare models", "evaluate FM", "human evaluation", "which model is best"
vs: Model Monitor watches models in production; Model Evaluation compares models before choosing.

what: Purchased, dedicated model units giving guaranteed throughput for a base or custom model, optionally with a 1-month or 6-month commitment.
use: run inference on a fine-tuned custom model in Bedrock
guarantee consistent high throughput for a production workload
not: Experiment cheaply with no commitment (use On-Demand)
Process a large one-time offline job at a discount (use batch inference)
vs: On-Demand = pay per token; Batch = ~50% cheaper asynchronous jobs.

what: Free, no-code Amazon Bedrock playground for building, sharing and learning with generative AI apps.
use: let employees experiment with generative AI apps for free without an AWS account setup
learn prompt engineering in a hands-on, no-code way
not: Host a production application with enterprise security controls
Fine-tune a model on private data
vs: Bedrock console playground is in your AWS account; PartyRock is a free public playground.

what: Fully managed platform to build, train, tune, deploy and monitor your own machine learning models with any framework.
use: train a custom ML model with the team's own Python code and data
deploy a custom-built model to a managed, auto-scaling endpoint
not: Call a third-party foundation model by API with zero infrastructure (use Bedrock)
Add document text extraction without ML expertise (use Textract)
cue: "build, train and deploy custom models", "full control", "data scientists"
vs: Bedrock consumes FMs; SageMaker builds and hosts your own models.

what: ML hub of pre-trained models (including open-source foundation models) and solution templates that you can deploy or fine-tune in a few clicks on SageMaker endpoints in your own account and VPC.
use: quickly deploy an open-source LLM inside the company's own VPC
fine-tune an open-source model with the least effort using a ready-made training job
not: Use a model with no endpoints to manage at all (use Bedrock)
Label images (use Ground Truth)
vs: JumpStart = you host the endpoint; Bedrock = serverless.

what: No-code visual interface for business analysts to prepare data, build ML models (forecasting, classification, regression) and use ready-made and generative AI models.
use: let business analysts with no coding skills build a sales forecasting model
generate predictions from a spreadsheet through a point-and-click interface
not: Give data scientists full control of custom training code (use SageMaker Studio)
Run large-scale distributed FM pre-training (use HyperPod)
vs: Studio is for coders; Canvas is for analysts.

what: Visual data preparation inside SageMaker: import, clean, transform and analyze data with 300+ built-in transforms and a data-quality report, then export to pipelines.
use: clean and transform data for ML in SageMaker with minimal code
generate a data quality and insights report before training
not: Label raw images (use Ground Truth)
Store features for reuse across teams (use Feature Store)
vs: Glue DataBrew is the general-purpose (non-SageMaker) equivalent.

what: Data labeling service: human labeling workflows using your own workers, Amazon Mechanical Turk or vendors, with active learning to auto-label. Ground Truth Plus provides an AWS-managed expert workforce.
use: create high-quality labeled training data for an image classification model
obtain labeled samples from a large unlabeled dataset using a public workforce
not: Review low-confidence predictions in production (use A2I)
Detect bias in a dataset (use Clarify)
vs: Ground Truth labels training data; A2I reviews predictions.

what: Central repository to create, store, share and reuse ML features with an online store (low-latency inference) and offline store (training).
use: share and reuse feature definitions across multiple data science teams
keep features consistent between training and real-time inference
not: Store raw documents for RAG (use S3 + Knowledge Bases)
Version trained models (use Model Registry)
vs: Model Registry stores models; Feature Store stores features.

what: Detects bias in data (pre-training) and in model predictions (post-training), and explains predictions with SHAP feature attributions and partial dependence plots. Also evaluates FMs.
use: check whether a loan model treats applicants of different ages fairly
explain to regulators which features drove an individual prediction
not: Block toxic chatbot output at runtime (use Guardrails)
Document the model's intended use (use Model Cards)
vs: Clarify explains and measures bias; Model Monitor alerts on drift over time.

what: Continuously monitors deployed models for data quality drift, model quality drift, bias drift and feature-attribution drift against a baseline, with CloudWatch alerts.
use: get alerted when production input data starts to differ from training data
detect when a deployed model's accuracy degrades over time
not: Compare FMs before choosing one (use Bedrock Model Evaluation)
Label data (use Ground Truth)
vs: Debugger watches training; Model Monitor watches production.

what: Documentation records for your models: intended uses, risk rating, training data and details, evaluation results and ethical considerations, for governance and audits.
use: document a model's intended use and limitations for auditors
record which dataset trained a model for governance
not: Learn how AWS designed its own AI services (use AWS AI Service Cards)
Measure bias automatically (use Clarify)
vs: Model Cards = your models; AI Service Cards = AWS's services.

what: Catalog of model versions with metadata, lineage and approval status, used to promote approved models to production in CI/CD.
use: track model versions and approve only validated models for deployment
not: Share features across teams (use Feature Store)
Build no-code models (use Canvas)
vs: Pipelines orchestrates; Registry stores versions.

what: Purpose-built workflow orchestration for MLOps: define repeatable DAGs of processing, training, evaluation and registration steps.
use: automate retraining and deployment of models as a repeatable CI/CD workflow
not: Visualize data quality (use Data Wrangler)
vs: Step Functions is general workflow; Pipelines is ML-native.

what: Resilient, managed clusters for large-scale distributed training of foundation models, with automatic fault detection and recovery.
use: pre-train a large foundation model across thousands of accelerators for weeks
not: Let analysts build models without code (use Canvas)
vs: Regular training jobs are fine for small models.

what: Adds human review workflows to ML predictions: route low-confidence or sensitive results from Textract, Rekognition or custom models to human reviewers.
use: have humans review document-extraction results whose confidence is below 80%
add human oversight to high-stakes model decisions
not: Label raw training data at scale (use Ground Truth)
vs: Ground Truth = before training; A2I = after prediction.

what: Natural language processing on text: sentiment, entities, key phrases, language detection, topic modeling, PII detection and redaction, custom classification and custom entities.
use: analyze the sentiment of thousands of customer reviews
detect and redact PII in support tickets
classify documents into custom business categories
not: Extract text from scanned images (use Textract first)
Generate new marketing copy (use Bedrock)
vs: Comprehend analyzes text; Textract extracts text from documents; Bedrock generates text.

what: HIPAA-eligible NLP that extracts medical entities (conditions, medications, dosages, tests, PHI) and relationships from unstructured clinical text.
use: extract diagnoses and medications from doctors' notes
not: Transcribe doctor-patient audio (use Transcribe Medical)
vs: Transcribe Medical turns speech into text; Comprehend Medical understands it.

what: Extracts printed and handwritten text, forms (key-value pairs), tables and signatures from scanned documents and PDFs; supports queries and specialized APIs for invoices, receipts and IDs.
use: digitize handwritten forms and tables from scanned insurance claims
extract fields from invoices and receipts
not: Determine sentiment of the extracted text (use Comprehend)
Detect objects in photos (use Rekognition)
vs: Rekognition finds text in natural images; Textract understands document structure.

what: Computer vision for images and video: object and scene labels, face detection and comparison, celebrity recognition, text in images, unsafe-content moderation, PPE detection, and Custom Labels.
use: automatically moderate user-uploaded images for unsafe content
identify objects and animals in a photo library
verify a user's identity by comparing faces
not: Extract tables from a scanned PDF (use Textract)
Generate new images from text (use Bedrock image models)
vs: Rekognition analyzes images; Nova Canvas/Titan Image generate them.

what: Automatic speech recognition: converts speech to text in batch or streaming, with speaker diarization, custom vocabularies, PII redaction, Call Analytics and Transcribe Medical.
use: generate subtitles for videos
transcribe customer service calls for later analysis
not: Read text aloud (use Polly)
Translate text to another language (use Translate)
vs: Transcribe = ears; Polly = mouth.

what: Text-to-speech: turns text into lifelike speech in many voices and languages, with SSML, neural and generative voices, and lexicons.
use: make an e-learning platform read lessons aloud
give an app a spoken voice response
not: Convert speech into text (use Transcribe)
vs: Polly speaks; Transcribe listens.

what: Neural machine translation between languages, real time or batch, with custom terminology.
use: translate product descriptions into 10 languages
translate chat messages between agents and customers in real time
not: Detect the sentiment of text (use Comprehend)
Convert audio to text (use Transcribe)
vs: Translate converts language; Comprehend detects language.

what: Builds conversational interfaces (voice and text chatbots) with intents, slots and fulfillment via Lambda; the same technology as Alexa. Integrates with Amazon Connect.
use: build a voice bot in a contact center that collects a customer's account number and books appointments
create a text chatbot with structured intents for ordering
not: Search enterprise documents to find answers (use Kendra or Q Business)
Generate long-form content (use Bedrock)
vs: Lex = structured conversational flows; Bedrock = open-ended generation.

what: ML-powered intelligent enterprise search across documents and data sources with natural-language queries; can serve as the retriever in RAG.
use: let employees search across SharePoint, S3 and Confluence with natural-language questions
retrieve relevant passages from company documents for a RAG application
not: Generate new text (pair with an FM)
Store vector embeddings for custom similarity search (use OpenSearch)
vs: Kendra is a managed search engine; OpenSearch is a search/vector database you configure.

what: Fully managed recommendation engine using your interaction data (same technology as Amazon.com), with real-time personalization.
use: show personalized product recommendations to each website visitor
rank content in a user's feed based on behavior
not: Forecast next quarter's demand (use Forecast or Canvas)
vs: Personalize recommends; Forecast predicts time series.

what: Managed time-series forecasting (demand, inventory, resource planning). New customers are directed to SageMaker Canvas for forecasting.
use: predict product demand for the next 12 weeks from historical sales
not: Recommend products to a user (use Personalize)
vs: Canvas now covers no-code forecasting.

what: Managed service to build fraud-detection models from your historical events, such as online payments and new account sign-ups.
use: flag potentially fraudulent online transactions and fake account registrations
not: Detect malicious activity in AWS accounts (use GuardDuty)
vs: GuardDuty = threats to your AWS account; Fraud Detector = business fraud.

what: Generative AI assistant for employees that answers questions, summarizes and creates content grounded in enterprise data via 40+ connectors, respecting existing user permissions.
use: give employees a chat assistant that answers from internal wikis and SharePoint with the least development effort
not: Help developers write code in an IDE (use Q Developer)
Build a public customer-facing chatbot with full control of the model (use Bedrock)
vs: Q Business is ready-made; Bedrock Knowledge Bases is the build-your-own option.

what: Generative AI assistant for software development: code suggestions in the IDE and CLI, chat about AWS, security scanning, reference tracking for open-source code, and code transformation (e.g. Java upgrades).
use: increase developer productivity with code generation in the IDE
upgrade legacy Java applications automatically
not: Answer HR questions from company documents (use Q Business)
vs: Q Developer codes; Q Business answers employee questions.

what: Generative BI: ask questions about data in natural language, build visuals and dashboards, and create executive summaries and data stories.
use: let business users ask natural-language questions about sales dashboards
not: Train ML models (use SageMaker)
vs: QuickSight = BI; Q adds gen-AI.

what: Managed search and analytics engine (incl. Serverless) with a vector engine supporting k-NN similarity search; the default vector store for Bedrock Knowledge Bases.
use: store document embeddings and run semantic similarity search for RAG
not: Run relational transactions for an ordering system (use RDS/Aurora)
vs: Aurora/RDS PostgreSQL with pgvector is the relational vector option.

what: Relational database that stores and searches vector embeddings with the pgvector extension, alongside regular relational data.
use: add vector similarity search to an existing PostgreSQL application for RAG
not: Generate embeddings itself (use an embedding model such as Titan Embeddings)
vs: OpenSearch is the search-native vector option.

what: Object storage that holds training data, documents for RAG and model artifacts, with encryption, versioning, access policies and lifecycle rules.
use: store a data lake of training data with lifecycle rules that delete data after a retention period
not: Run similarity search on embeddings (use a vector store)
vs: S3 stores; OpenSearch searches vectors.

what: Serverless data integration (ETL) with the Glue Data Catalog for metadata; Glue DataBrew offers visual no-code data preparation.
use: build ETL jobs that prepare raw data for ML training
catalog the schemas of datasets in a data lake
not: Label images (use Ground Truth)
vs: Data Wrangler is SageMaker's visual prep.

what: Crowdsourcing marketplace of a public on-demand human workforce, used by Ground Truth and A2I for labeling and review of non-confidential data.
use: cheaply label large volumes of non-confidential data with a public workforce
not: Label confidential medical data (use a private workforce)
vs: Use private or vendor workforces for sensitive data.

what: 1/18-scale autonomous race car and simulator for learning reinforcement learning hands-on.
use: teach a team reinforcement learning concepts through a hands-on racing simulator
not: Build a production recommender (use Personalize)

what: AWS-designed ML chips: Trainium (Trn instances) for cost-efficient training; Inferentia (Inf instances) for low-cost, high-throughput inference.
use: reduce the cost of running deep learning inference at scale (Inferentia)
reduce the cost of training large models (Trainium)
not: Serve a model with no infrastructure management (use Bedrock or serverless endpoints)
vs: INFerentia = INFerence; TRAINium = TRAINing.

what: Controls who can access which AWS resources: users, groups, roles and least-privilege policies (including who can invoke specific Bedrock models).
use: ensure only the data science team can invoke a specific Bedrock model
grant the Bedrock service role permission to read an S3 bucket
not: Record the history of API calls (use CloudTrail)
vs: IAM grants; CloudTrail records.

what: Creates and manages encryption keys (AWS managed or customer managed) used to encrypt data at rest across S3, SageMaker and Bedrock; key use is logged in CloudTrail.
use: encrypt training data and custom models with customer managed keys
not: Discover PII in S3 (use Macie)
vs: Secrets Manager stores credentials; KMS manages keys.

what: Uses ML to discover and classify sensitive data such as PII and financial data in Amazon S3 buckets.
use: find which S3 buckets used for training contain personal data
not: Redact PII inside a chatbot response (use Guardrails or Comprehend)
Scan EC2 for vulnerabilities (use Inspector)
vs: Macie finds; Comprehend/Guardrails redact.

what: Records API activity in your account (who, what, when, from where), including denied attempts and Bedrock/SageMaker calls, for auditing.
use: identify which user tried to invoke a Bedrock model without permission
audit all API actions on AI resources
not: Track configuration changes and compliance rules (use Config)
Log full prompt and response text (use Bedrock invocation logging)
cue: "who made the API call", "audit trail", "unauthorized attempts"
vs: CloudTrail = actions; Config = configuration state.

what: Records resource configurations over time and evaluates them against compliance rules (e.g. encryption enabled, endpoints not public).
use: continuously check that all SageMaker notebooks have encryption enabled
not: Find out who invoked an API (use CloudTrail)
vs: Config = state over time; CloudTrail = API events.

what: Monitoring service for metrics, logs and alarms; receives Bedrock invocation logs and metrics such as latency and invocations.
use: alarm when a model endpoint's latency exceeds a threshold
not: Download compliance reports (use Artifact)

what: Self-service portal for AWS security and compliance reports (SOC, ISO, PCI) and agreements, including third-party ISV reports with email notifications.
use: download AWS's SOC 2 report for an auditor
get notified when an ISV's compliance report is available
not: Collect evidence about your own resources (use Audit Manager)
vs: Artifact = AWS's reports; Audit Manager = your evidence.

what: Continuously collects evidence from your AWS usage and maps it to frameworks (including a generative AI best-practices framework) to simplify audits.
use: prepare continuously for an audit of AI workloads against a compliance framework
not: Download AWS's own ISO certificates (use Artifact)

what: Best-practice checks across cost optimization, security, performance, fault tolerance and service limits, e.g. idle or underutilized resources.
use: find underutilized Amazon Comprehend endpoints to cut cost
not: Record API calls (use CloudTrail)

what: Intelligent threat detection that analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs for malicious or anomalous activity.
use: detect compromised credentials or unusual API activity in the account
not: Find software vulnerabilities in containers (use Inspector)

what: Automated vulnerability management that scans EC2, container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities and network exposure.
use: scan the containers that host a model for known CVEs
not: Find PII in S3 (use Macie)

what: Private connectivity from a VPC to AWS services (such as Bedrock and SageMaker) through interface VPC endpoints, without traversing the internet.
use: call Bedrock from a VPC that has no internet access to meet regulatory rules
not: Encrypt data at rest (use KMS)

what: Data management service to catalog, discover, share and govern data across an organization with a business data catalog.
use: let teams discover and request governed access to datasets for ML
not: Set column-level permissions in a data lake directly (Lake Formation)
vs: Lake Formation enforces fine-grained data lake permissions.

what: Builds and secures data lakes with centralized fine-grained (table, column, row) permissions on data cataloged in Glue.
use: restrict ML engineers to only non-sensitive columns of a training table
not: Detect PII automatically (use Macie)
